fields.meaning: To the end, persistently, absolutely (あくまでも)
examples: This is purely my own personal opinion.
He persistently maintained his innocence.
We will proceed exactly according to plan, no matter what.

fields.meaning: Truly…, really looks very… (いかにも)
examples: He talks just like a scholar.
They're wearing a watch that looks really expensive.
They looked truly disappointed.

fields.meaning: Already…, no longer… (もはや)
examples: It's already too late.
That technology is already outdated.
There is no longer anyone who can stop him.

fields.meaning: How…!, What a…! (exclamation: なんという/なんて)
examples: What a beautiful view!
What a kind person!
What on earth have you done!

fields.meaning: Surely…, must have been… (さぞ)
examples: Raising a child on your own must have been very hard.
Your parents must have been overjoyed at the news that you passed.
It must be very cold at the top of the mountain.

fields.meaning: Especially…, above all… (とりわけ)
examples: This summer is especially hot.
He is good at languages, especially pronunciation.
What made the strongest impression on me was the last scene.

fields.meaning: If luck is on your side…, with any luck… (hoping for a chance)
examples: With any luck, I'd like to win the championship.
I went to the party thinking that, with any luck, I might get to see her.
Trying to get it for free if you can get away with it — how shameless.

fields.meaning: Regardless of… (formal written language)
examples: Violence cannot be tolerated, whatever the reason.
Regardless of the result, there is meaning in having given it your all.
Anyone can apply, regardless of experience.

fields.meaning: Probably…, surely… (archaic form of だろう: 良かろう)
fields.connection: Aい (drop い) + かろう (良かろう)
examples: That should be fine.
Going alone would probably be dangerous.
The sea in winter must be very cold.

fields.meaning: Go ahead and… (command to an inferior; dramatic/novel style)
examples: If you're so frustrated, go ahead and come at me.
If you want to go, then go.
Let those who want to laugh, laugh.

fields.meaning: Leaving things as they are… (着たなりで寝る)
examples: He fell asleep with his coat still on.
Don't come into the room with your shoes still on.
I went out and left the light on.

fields.meaning: Speaking of… (extreme degree; indescribable)
examples: The beauty of the sunrise seen from Mt. Fuji was beyond words.
The embarrassment I felt then was indescribable.
His room is so messy that there's nowhere to set foot.

fields.meaning: Should I call it… or… (hesitating over how to put it)
fields.connection: [expression A] + といおうか、[expression B] + といおうか
examples: He's honest, or maybe simple — he says whatever he thinks right away.
Bold or reckless, I'm not sure which, but his plan surprised me.
I'm happy, or maybe embarrassed — I have mixed feelings.

fields.meaning: If…, then (it has its own difficulties/way)
fields.connection: NならNで / VたらVたで（repeating the same word）
examples: If it's small, well, it's small — but with a little ingenuity it becomes easy to live in.
If you don't have money, you don't have money — somehow things work out.
Now that I have free time, I don't know what to do with it.

fields.meaning: Worthy of…, living up to…
examples: It was a splendid performance, worthy of a champion.
I will work hard so as to live up to the name of my alma mater.
I want to live a life I would not be ashamed of before my own conscience.

fields.meaning: Dared to…, damn… (vulgar, contemptuous)
examples: That bastard stole my money.
Calling me at this hour, damn it.
Damn rain, it's started again.

fields.meaning: To force (someone) to…, leaving no choice
examples: The typhoon forced residents to evacuate.
A lack of funds forced a change in the plan.
The recession is forcing many shops to close.

fields.meaning: Having a hidden story, having one's own reasons (訳あり商品)
fields.connection: 訳あり + の + N / 訳あって + [sentence/clause]
examples: This store sells "special-reason" goods (slightly flawed, leftover stock, etc.) cheaply.
Those two seem to have some kind of complicated relationship.
For personal reasons, I'm living at my parents' home now.

fields.meaning: Whether … or not … (expresses that two contrasting possibilities do not change the result)
Extremely, intensely, to the max, completely (colloquial emphatic prefix 「ガン」; e.g. ガン見 = to stare hard)
To do (something) for a person/animal of lower status than oneself; also used to show irritation, deliberately doing something the other person dislikes
examples: I bought my child a new bicycle, and it was stolen the very next day.
This year again, I sent my younger brother in Tokyo some specialties from our hometown.
When I let the dog off the leash in the big park, it ran around looking happy.
A company with pay this low — I'll quit any time I feel like it.

A: If your bag is heavy, I'll carry it for you.
B: Oh, no, it's fine.

A: Someone like you should just drop dead.
B: If you're going to say that, I really will die, just to show you.
fields.explain: Expresses that the speaker (or someone on the speaker's side) does something for the sake of a person of lower status than the speaker, or for an animal. As in 5. and 6., it is sometimes also used as an expression of anger, meaning to do something the other person dislikes. For someone on an equal footing with the speaker, 「Ｖ－てあげる」 is used. (２８６)

fields.meaning: …that, saying that… (modifies a noun of speech/thought; formal written language)
examples: I received a reply from my former teacher saying that he could not attend the wedding.
A student has expressed the wish to take a year's leave of absence in order to study abroad.
On this matter, everyone agreed with the chair's proposal that it be referred to the next deliberation.
I received an official order to transfer to the Sapporo branch for one year starting next month.
The Minister of Education stated the view that, in order to improve school education, a radical reform of the entrance examination system of higher education institutions is necessary.
fields.explain:
A clause expressing the content of speech or thought modifies a noun; used in a formal style. For Ｎ, nouns related to speech acts such as 「手紙、返事、依頼、提案、警告、命令」, or to thinking such as 「意見、見解、考え、希望」, are used. It is used when talking about other people's statements or thoughts; when expressing the speaker's own thoughts, 「という」 rather than 「との」 is normally used, as in the following example.
*（例） 私は夫婦別姓を合法化すべきだという意見をもっている。

fields.meaning: Expresses confirmation; evaluation
examples: A pasokon is a small computer that an individual can use.
Renge means the lotus flower.
What kind of welfare system will be required in 21st-century Japan?
"Universal" means applying broadly and generally in every case.
What on earth is family to me?
fields.explain: Takes a noun and is used to state what its meaning, nature or content is like. It is used to state an essential characteristic in forms such as 「とは…ものだ」, or to define the meaning or content of a word or phrase in forms such as …とは…のことだ／意味だ」「…とは…ということだ／意味だ」. It is a written-language expression; in spoken language 「Ｎというのは」 is more common.

fields.meaning: It's not that … not (…); somewhat feeling that way
examples: I do, to some extent, admit that I was partly at fault too.
Come to think of it, I kind of feel that his opinion makes sense too.

A: Do you like natto?
B: It's not that I don't eat it, but I don't like it very much.

A: Come on, let's go.
B: Well, if you insist, I might go.
fields.explain: Attaches to the negative form of a verb and expresses that such an action or perception can sometimes hold true. When verbs related to thought or perception such as 「言う、考える、思う、認める、感じる、気がする」 are used, it means "somehow I get that feeling."

fields.meaning: If it were …, it would be acceptable, but …
fields.connection: N + ならまだしも / plain form + ならまだしも

fields.meaning: Expresses something that does not match expectations
examples: Even in difficult circumstances, he keeps working hard without giving in.
Even in a warm family, her heart was not fulfilled.
Even on her deathbed, my mother kept wishing for her children's happiness.
fields.explain: Takes a noun and means "even though placed in the situation expressed there." It is followed by something that differs from what would be expected to happen in that situation. Written language.

fields.meaning: For (that person), from (that person's) point of view
examples: Which songs are popular right now doesn't matter at all to me. There are tons of more important things than that.
I gave her an old computer I hadn't used for a long time, and it seems she was very grateful for it — she thanked me again and again.
I was talking casually, but for him it was probably a big problem. He became depressed and stopped talking to anyone.

For my mother, it must have been a great shock since the son she had raised so lovingly suddenly left home, but I felt like cheering on my younger brother, who was trying to become independent from our parents.
fields.explain: Attaches to a noun referring to a person and means "for that person." Used when you want to say that the person has a different view compared to others. 「…にしてみたら」 can also be used. (４３９)

fields.meaning: Being convinced/assuming that … (but in reality it is not so)
examples: I had assumed skiing was difficult, but when I tried it, it was easy.
I was sure I had corrected all the mistakes, but I was told there were still a few.
I assumed there'd be no class tomorrow because of the strike, so I didn't prepare for class at all.
I had assumed the classics were boring, but when I read them, they were surprisingly interesting.
Assuming that Mr. Yoshida wasn't coming, I made food for only 5 people.
fields.explain: Expresses the speaker's assumption. Normally used when the speaker had believed something to be true, but in reality it was not.

fields.meaning: What with … and … (emphatic listing, with a nuance of complaint)

fields.name: question word＋にしたって
examples: Either way, there is almost no chance of winning.
Whatever you do, it costs money.
Nobody wants to get involved in a problem like this.
In any case, it takes time to solve this kind of problem.
fields.explain: Used with question words such as 「いずれ」「どちら」「なに」「だれ」, it means "in any case" or "no matter who." As in 2., a clause containing a question word may also be used. It is the casual spoken-language version of 「…にしても」. (４３６)

fields.connection: かつて + [clause] / かつて + の + N
examples: This area was once a famous rice-producing region.
I hear she once stayed in Japan as a special correspondent for a newspaper.
If an earthquake were to occur in this region next time, there is a fear that it would be on an unprecedented scale…
When I saw him for the first time in a long while, he had gotten as fat as a sumo wrestler, and there was no trace of the lean, sharp athlete he once was.
Never before has our country depended on foreign countries for the production of rice, our staple food.
fields.explain: Means 「以前」 (before) or 「昔」 (long ago). It is sometimes also said 「かって」. In a negative expression, as in 「かつてない」 in 3. and 5., it means "never even once until now." 「かつてない」 and 「未だかつて…ない」 are set phrases. Written language. (７９)

examples: The moment I stood up, the house shook violently.
The very moment the prince kissed the sleeping princess, the spell was broken.
The moment I found out I had failed the exam, everything went black before my eyes, and I could feel the blood draining from my face.
This is the moment of birth.
fields.explain: Means 「ちょうどその時」 (just at that time). It rarely attaches to nouns. In spoken language, 「Ｖ－たとたん」 is used. (１４５)

examples: It's a small company, but it makes a reasonable profit.
If they say they don't like it, they probably have their own reasons.
The children are also working hard together in their own way.
If you make an effort, you should get results to match.
fields.explain: Implies that the thing has limits or shortcomings, and means "suitable to it, while acknowledging that." (４０７)

fields.meaning: Expresses irrelevance
examples: Whether they are sick or elderly, the enemy attacks without any consideration.
Even if you are healthy, once you are past middle age you should have regular checkups.
Even an eminent monk sometimes cannot cut off his doubts.
fields.explain: A somewhat old-fashioned way of saying 「Ｎ／Ｎａであっても」.
fields.notes: Attaches to conjugating words and expresses the same meaning as 「ても」. Because it is a literary usage, it sounds more old-fashioned than 「ても」.

examples: His modern architecture, combined with the magnificent natural scenery in the background, creates a simple and tranquil space.
In that film, the sound of inexpensive instruments combines with beautiful images to make a wonderful work that cannot fail to move viewers.
His originality, combined with her traditional beauty, makes the furniture they create full of originality.
fields.explain: Attaches to a noun and means "that thing interacting with another element" or "its qualities working together with the qualities of another element." A written-language expression. (２９３)

fields.meaning: If you let (that person) say it…, according to (that person)… (に言わせると)

examples: It is not hard to imagine that if inflation continues like this, social unrest will increase and the foundation of the government will be put at risk.
It is not hard to imagine that Taro, abandoned by both his parents and his teachers, was probably on the verge of seeking salvation in an invitation from a delinquent group.
Why he resorted to such behavior is not hard to understand if you listen carefully to the circumstances before and after the incident.
fields.explain: Normally used idiomatically in the form 「想像／理解にかたくない」, meaning that something can easily be imagined, or is obvious to anyone who thinks about it. A stiff, written-language expression. (４３１)

fields.meaning: Expresses addition
fields.explain:
のみか means The grammar point ～のみか is used to indicate that not only the first mentioned fact is true, but also an additional, often more surprising or significant fact is true. It can be translated as 'not only... but also...' or 'as well as...'.

Structure: Noun + のみか

～のみか is a formal conjunction used to connect two related facts, emphasizing that the second fact is an additional or even more serious matter than the first. It is often used in written or formal contexts to express that something is true not only in one aspect but also in another, sometimes unexpected, aspect. In the example sentence, it shows that due to the disaster, the person lost not only property but also close family members.

examples: I'm counting on you.
There's something I'd like you to do for me.
Could you do me a favor?
Well, let's give it a try.
Why don't I go along with the idea?
Please, have one.
fields.explain: Used idiomatically in everyday spoken language. It means "a little, as a try." It is used when asking someone for something, as in 1. ～3., or when trying something out, as in 4. and 5. 6. and ⑦ are used when offering food or the like to someone. (５０６)

fields.name: もあろう（counter＋もあろう）
fields.meaning: Expresses emphasis | how large or small an amount is
fields.explain:
もあろう（数量詞＋もあろう） means Indicates a surprisingly large quantity or amount, emphasizing that the number or amount is unexpectedly or impressively high.

Structure: 数量詞＋もあろう

The expression 'もあろう' is used after a numerical quantifier to emphasize the magnitude or extent of something. It often conveys a sense of surprise or emphasis on the large quantity, suggesting that the amount is notable or significant. For example, '2メートルもあろう' means 'as much as 2 meters' or 'about 2 meters, which is quite large.' This grammar point is typically used in written or formal contexts to highlight the size or amount.
